root_cause.text: The KVM SEV driver omitted a check for whether a vCPU has already been launched (i.e., its VMSA is encrypted) before allowing a VMSA synchronization operation (`sev_es_sync_vmsa`), which on SNP-capable hosts causes a write to guest-private memory and triggers an RMP violation page fault, leading to a host panic.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an explicit guard `if (vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected) return -EINVAL;` at the start of `sev_es_sync_vmsa`. The commit message confirms that the flaw allowed VMSA sync after launch, and on SNP hosts this results in an RMP #PF and host panic, as shown in the call trace where `sev_es_sync_vmsa` is invoked from `snp_launch_finish` after the VMSA has already been encrypted.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to return -EINVAL in sev_es_sync_vmsa when guest state is already protected, preventing double protection.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check at the start of sev_es_sync_vmsa that returns -EINVAL if vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected is true.
intent_record.how: The function will now immediately abort with an error when called on a VCPU whose guest state is already marked protected, preventing any further processing of the VMSA synchronization.
